answer: Make every identity climb one ridge at a time: a new agent starts on a low ledge with no privileges, and each epoch of honest, peer-attested work lifts it one step higher toward the horizon of full trust. The climb is a hash chain of its own past work, one link per epoch, bound to its key and impossible to copy or buy. A fake that jumps straight to the top is exposed, because its chain is empty. To field a thousand trusted fakes, an attacker must climb a thousand ridges in parallel, paying months of real work per identity, while honest agents keep the height they already earned.
